correctness.rationale: Every maximum-count circular window can be shifted to begin on a one. For any of the three one-rooted cuts the second and third occurrence thresholds are exactly g_i+2 and n-g_(i-1). A single cut maximizes counts at every length iff it simultaneously minimizes those thresholds, namely the following gap is minimum and preceding gap is maximum. Distinct triples admit two cyclic orderings and only one is forbidden. The substitution a=t, b=t+1+u, c=t+2+u+v gives n=6+3t+2u+v and the rational generating function. The at-most-two-one/zero lemma proves global minimal length six. Unbounded results are proved symbolically; standalone exhaustive checker independently validates all binary words to 11 and all three-one words to 41.

originality.rationale: The primary 2011 and 2014 prefix-normal articles concern all ordinary linear factors, generating and testing words, and realizing factor maxima by potentially new words. They do not classify which existing cyclic rotations realize all maxima of wrapping circular factors. Their linear gap inequalities are structurally relevant but do not by themselves state the two-orientation obstruction, exact generating function or asymptotic half of weight-three necklaces. The published linearly prefix-normal word 110010 is a direct witness that ordinary prefix-normality does not imply the cyclic property. Targeted query searches found no covering statement; unindexed historical results are a residual priority risk.

value.rationale: The all-length necklace classification answers when an existing circular sequence admits a cut simultaneously representing the maximum number of ones in every window length, a natural restriction of the jumbled-index normal-form problem. It identifies the global sharp first failure at six, complete weight-three obstructions by orientation, a rational generating function and asymptotic failure prevalence one-half. This provides a natural exact structural classification beyond an isolated finite computation.
